title: dedicated-autoscaler: tokenbucket smoothing + throughput guarantees + utilization reporting
author: Ethan Zhao
release_notes: Adds token-bucket smoothing to the Dedicated autoscaler to reduce oscillations; changes throughput guarantee calculation to include burst credits; exposes fleet_util_sma utilization metric. Backwards compatible.
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated fleets observed oscillatory scaling when traffic has short high-frequency bursts (e.g. periodic batch jobs + steady tail). This PR implements a token-bucket smoothing layer and updates throughput-guarantee accounting so burst credits are considered in SLA calculations. It also adds an experimental fleet_util_sma (moving average) metric to improve capacity planning and alerting.

Summary of changes: 1) Add token-bucket smoothing policy in the autoscaler controller to damp rapid up/down decisions while preserving short-term burst capacity; 2) Adjust throughput guarantee calculation to include available burst credits so reported guarantees better reflect real serving behavior; 3) Emit fleet_util_sma (30s and 5m variants) and surface the metric in the console; 4) Add unit and e2e tests, update docs and migration notes; 5) Rollout plan with canary, gradual ramp, and automatic rollback on regressions.

Design details: The smoothing layer maintains a per-fleet token bucket where tokens accumulate proportional to provisioned throughput and are spent when observed instantaneous demand exceeds the baseline. The autoscaler consults both the smoothed demand and raw instantaneous queue depth: scale-ups require sustained demand above threshold or token consumption to preserve low-latency bursts; scale-downs are gated by the SMA to avoid removing capacity prematurely. Throughput guarantees now compute effective_capacity = provisioned + min(burst_credits, burst_window * provisioned_rate) for reporting and SLO math. Metrics: fleet_util_sma_30s, fleet_util_sma_5m (percent), autoscaler_tokenbucket_fill (ratio), autoscaler_tokenbucket_spend (count).

Testing: Unit tests included for token bucket arithmetic and guarantee formula; integration tests simulate mixed steady+burst workloads to validate reduced oscillation and maintained tail latency under burst scenarios. CI initially failed on a flaky e2e (timing-sensitive), addressed by increasing test harness tolerance and adding deterministic seeds. Performance bench shows median scale decision frequency reduced by ~45% under synthetic burst workload and p99 latency held within SLOs.

Rollout: Canary deploy to 5% of Dedicated fleets for 48h, monitor fleet_util_sma and scale event rates, then 25% for 24h, full rollout if no regressions. Automatic rollback if increased scale churn or >1% of requests incur latency regression beyond configured thresholds.

Migration notes: Backwards compatible: controller will default to previous behavior when smoothing is disabled (feature flag). Customers using custom autoscaler hooks should verify they don't rely on immediate scale-downs.
